critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to ~865 lines with 30+ routes; split into routers/{auth,orders,ratings,admin,email}.py + services/{email,twilio,ratings}.py before iteration 4.

weekly_summary_loop() runs a full users scan every hour with no cursor/backoff. When user count grows, add pagination and a per-user lock/dedupe key (e.g., week_year_iso) to prevent duplicate sends if loop overlaps a Sunday hour boundary.

GET /orders/mine still does an extra query for collector ratings but is fine (batched via $in). Ensure db.users has index on {role:1, avg_rating:-1, ratings_count:-1} for /collectors/top and on {referral_code:1} unique.
PATCH /user/email lacks uniqueness check — two users can share the same email (weekly loop will still send to each). Consider a soft-unique index or explicit 409.
recompute_collector_rating scans all ratings on each new rating (fine for now, will blow up at scale) — could store running sum/count on the user doc and $inc.
render_weekly_summary_html is a 40-line f-string inside server.py — extract to templates/weekly_summary.html for maintainability.
No test / no endpoint to view or delete an individual rating (admin cannot moderate). Not a blocker but worth noting.
